questions.stem: Is it heating or cooling? Sort the changes.
questions.explanation: Ice melts, an egg cooks and water boils when they are heated. Water freezes, jelly sets and melted chocolate goes hard when they are cooled.

questions.stem: An ice cube sits in the hot sun. What will it become?
questions.explanation: Heat melts ice into water.

questions.stem: Which picture shows something that melts in the sun?
questions.explanation: Ice cream melts when it gets warm. A rock and a coin do not melt in the sun.

questions.stem: Which can melt when heated? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Ice, chocolate and ice cream melt when they are heated. A brick and a key do not melt in everyday heat.

questions.stem: Water boils and turns to steam.
questions.explanation: When water is heated until it boils, it turns into steam.

questions.stem: This egg is cooked. It can turn back into a raw egg.
questions.image_alt: A fried egg in a pan.
questions.explanation: A cooked egg cannot go back. Cooking is a change that cannot go back.

questions.stem: Water turns into ice when it is ___.
questions.explanation: Cooling water makes it freeze into ice.

questions.stem: Salt ___ in water and seems to disappear.
questions.explanation: Salt dissolves in water. It mixes in and seems to disappear.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Melt is solid to liquid. Freeze is liquid to solid. Dissolve is mixing into water and seeming to disappear. Boil is water turning to steam.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to make pitha.
sequence: Mix rice flour and water into dough.
Steam the pitha over hot water.
The dough turns into a firm cake.
questions.explanation: Grandma mixes flour and water into dough. She steams it over hot water. The dough turns into a firm cake.

questions.stem: Mina leaves butter in the hot sun. What happens?
questions.explanation: Heat melts butter.

questions.stem: Rina wants ice cubes for a drink. Where should she put water?
questions.explanation: Cooling water makes it freeze. A freezer is very cold.

questions.stem: Imran stirs sugar in his tea. What happens to the sugar?
questions.explanation: Sugar dissolves in hot tea. It mixes in and seems to disappear.

questions.stem: Only grown-ups use the stove and hot water.
questions.explanation: Stoves and hot water can burn us. Children ask a grown-up for help.

questions.stem: Joy puts melted chocolate in the fridge. It goes hard again.
questions.explanation: Cooling makes melted chocolate go hard again. This change can go back.

questions.stem: Steam rises from a hot drink. When steam cools, it turns into...
questions.explanation: Steam turns back into water drops when it cools.

questions.stem: Match each picture to what happens.
questions.explanation: Ice melts when heated. A fried egg cooks and goes hard. Water drops freeze into ice when cooled.

questions.stem: Why does ice cream melt on a hot day?
questions.model_answer: The hot day heats the ice cream, so it melts into a liquid.
questions.explanation: Heat from the air and sun warms the ice cream. A solid ice cream turns into a liquid.

questions.stem: Which things dissolve in water? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Salt and sugar dissolve in water. Sand, rice and coins do not.

questions.stem: Can the change go back? Sort the changes.
questions.explanation: Ice melting, chocolate melting and water freezing can go back. A cooked egg and steamed pitha cannot.

questions.stem: Melting times: sun 10 minutes, classroom 25, fridge 60. Where did ice melt fastest?
questions.explanation: The shortest time was in the sun, 10 minutes, so ice melted fastest there.

questions.stem: Fridge: 60 minutes. Sun: 10 minutes. How many more minutes in the fridge?
questions.explanation: 60 minus 10 is 50, so the ice took 50 minutes longer in the fridge.

questions.stem: Is it a fair test to use ice cubes of different sizes?
questions.explanation: Big ice cubes take longer to melt. For a fair test the ice cubes must be the same size.

questions.stem: Sand dissolves in water.
questions.explanation: Sand does not dissolve. It sinks to the bottom.
